title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
summary: Find the greatest sum along any nonempty simple path in the tree.
statement: Find the greatest sum along any nonempty simple path in the tree. The path follows parent-child edges and may start and end anywhere. Each node contributes its value once.

examples.explanation: The best nonempty path is the node −3 alone.

hints: Conceptual: A path can turn at its highest node. Extending it to a parent can keep only one branch.
Directional: Compute the best downward gain from each child, treating negative gains as zero when extending.
Implementation: Update the global answer with the node value plus both nonnegative child gains. Return the node value plus the larger child gain upward.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time. Iterative postorder with stored gains uses O(n) auxiliary space.
